page.title: Virtual event production cost guide
page.description: Learn the main cost drivers, platform models, crew needs, and timelines for virtual and hybrid events so you can budget accurately.
page.h1: What does virtual event production cost?
page.definition: Virtual event production cost is the total spend for platform licences, broadcast crew, accessibility services, backup streams and project management needed to deliver a live online or hybrid experience. It also covers speaker rehearsals, branded graphics, moderation, recording, editing and post‑event distribution.
page.quick_answer: Start by choosing a platform model that matches your audience size, then add a production crew for run‑of‑show, rehearsal and a backup stream; budget $2,500 to $7,500 for a moderated webinar and $10,000 to $50,000 for a summit.

sections.h2: Which platform pricing model fits my audience size?

blocks.p: Platform pricing falls into three models: per‑host licences sized by attendee capacity, self‑serve monthly plans, and annual contracts quoted by sales.

ul: Per‑host licences sized by attendee capacity (e.g., Zoom Webinars)
Annual contracts quoted by sales (e.g., ON24, Cvent, Bizzabo, Goldcast)

sections.h2: What production crew do I need for a webinar versus a summit?

blocks.p: A simple webinar can be run by one producer, while a summit or hybrid event needs a show caller, speaker manager, moderator and platform operator.

ul: Webinar: one producer handles run‑of‑show, rehearsal, backup stream
Summit: show caller, speaker manager, moderator, platform operator

sections.h2: How do I budget for accessibility, backup streams and post‑event assets?

blocks.p: Add line items for captioning, sign language, a redundant encoder, edited recording and short clips to the platform fee.

head: Item
Typical scope
rows: Full event video trimmed and branded

sections.h2: What timeline should I plan from brief to live?

blocks.p: Allow two to three weeks from brief to live for a webinar and six to eight weeks for a summit or online conference.

sections.h2: When should I schedule rehearsals and deliver the replay?

blocks.p: Run one full rehearsal on the real platform two to five days before and a technical check sixty minutes before going live; send the replay within 24 to 48 hours.

ul: Full rehearsal two to five days before event
Technical check sixty minutes before go‑live

faq.q: How much does a moderated webinar typically cost?
faq.a: A moderated webinar usually falls between $2,500 and $7,500 for production crew, platform licence, rehearsal, live moderation, backup stream and edited recording; the final figure depends on speaker count, accessibility needs and whether you use an existing platform licence and any custom branding.

faq.q: What drives the cost difference between a webinar and a summit?
faq.a: A summit adds multiple sessions, a show caller, speaker manager, platform operator, hybrid venue AV, extended rehearsal days and broader accessibility services; these extra workstreams raise the budget to $10,000 to $50,000 or more compared with a single‑session webinar and post‑event analytics.

faq.q: Do I need a separate production contract if I already have a platform licence?
faq.a: Yes, the platform licence covers software only; production covers crew, cameras, encoder, run‑of‑show, backup stream and post‑event editing, which are purchased separately or bundled through a production partner such as West Peek Productions and includes speaker rehearsal, branded graphics and moderation.

faq.q: What is the typical lead time for a hybrid conference?
faq.a: Plan a hybrid conference six to eight weeks out; lock the venue AV and the platform before the agenda is final, then run a full rehearsal two to five days before and a technical check sixty minutes before going live.
